arxiv-2007-12017.creator: Bui Ngoc Muoi, Ngai-Ching Wong
arxiv-2007-12017.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Bui Ngoc Muoi, Ngai-Ching Wong. Let S S be a semitopological semigroup, and let C C be a nonempty closed convex subset of a reflexive Banach space. Under some amenability conditions on S S , we provide existence results of fixed points for several Bregman nonexpansive type actions S × C → C S\times C\to C , ( s , x ) ↦ T s ​ x (s,x)\mapsto T_{s}x , of S S on C C .

arxiv-2108-09028.title: Sufficient criteria for stabilization properties in Banach spaces
arxiv-2108-09028.creator: Michela Egidi, Dennis Gallaun, Christian Seifert, Martin Tautenhahn
arxiv-2108-09028.description: Abstract We study abstract sufficient criteria for open-loop stabilizability of linear control systems in a Banach space with a bounded control operator, which build up and generalize a sufficient condition for null-controllability in Banach spaces given by an uncertainty principle and a dissipation estimate.

arxiv-2211-03221.title: Stressing Dynamic Loss Models
arxiv-2211-03221.creator: Emma Kroell, Silvana M. Pesenti, Sebastian Jaimungal
arxiv-2211-03221.description: Abstract Stress testing, and in particular, reverse stress testing, is a prominent exercise in risk management practice. Reverse stress testing, in contrast to (forward) stress testing, aims to find an alternative but plausible model such that under that alternative model, specific adverse stresses (i.e. constraints) are satisfied. Here, we propose a reverse stress testing framework for dynamic models.

arxiv-2303-11482.title: On the group of homeomorphisms of the Basilica
arxiv-2303-11482.creator: Yury A.Neretin
arxiv-2303-11482.description: Abstract We show that the group of all homeomorphisms of the Basilica fractal coincides with a group of transformations of a certain non-locally finite ribbon tree. Also, we show that Basilica Thompson group defined by Belk and Forrest is dense in the group of all orientation preserving homeomorphisms of the Basilica. 1. The Basilica.

arxiv-2410-22704.title: BKT phase transition in nanoporous films of superconducting NbN
arxiv-2410-22704.creator: A. Verma, R. Vedin, J. Jesudasan, J. Lidmar, I. Maccari, S. Bose
arxiv-2410-22704.description: Abstract We present a study of the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) transition in mildly disordered NbN nanoporous (NP) films. The measured superfluid stiffness, J s J_{s} , is found to be much lower than that predicted by considering the reduction in the geometric area.

arxiv-2511-19526.title: Perceptual Taxonomy: Evaluating and Guiding Hierarchical Scene Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
arxiv-2511-19526.creator: Jonathan Lee, Xingrui Wang, Jiawei Peng, Luoxin Ye, Zehan Zheng, Tiezheng Zhang, Tao Wang, Wufei Ma, Siyi Chen, Yu-Cheng Chou, Prakhar Kaushik, Alan Yuille

We propose Perceptual Taxonomy, a structured process of scene understanding that first recognizes objects and their spatial configurations, then infers task-relevant properties, such as material, affordance, and function to support goal-directed reasoning.

pmc-10526825.title: Optimal Design of Galvanic Vestibular Stimulation for Patients with Vestibulopathy and Cerebellar Disorders
pmc-10526825.creator: Thanh Tin Nguyen, Seung-Beop Lee, Jin-Ju Kang, Sun-Young Oh, Lorenzo Rocchi
pmc-10526825.description: Objectives: Galvanic vestibular stimulation (GVS) has shown positive outcomes in various neurological and psychiatric disorders, such as enhancing postural balance and cognitive functions. pmc-11656659.creator: Xin Chai, Juan Zhang, Yachen Wang, Di Li, Dongli Zhu, Kaipeng Liang, Chunyu Yang, Jinping Wang, Qiuhong Gong, Zhiwei Yang, Ruitai Shao

pmc-11716106.creator: Nathan Friedman, Inbal Itzhak, Philippe Desmarais, John D Fisk, Linda Lee, Alexandre Henri‐Bhargava, Jacqueline Pettersen, Paula M McLaughlin, Zahinoor Ismail, Vladimir Khanassov, Morris Freedman, Howard Chertkow, Richard Camicioli, Megan E O'Connell, Maiya R Geddes
pmc-11716106.description: BackgroundRemote diagnostic assessment of cognitively impaired individuals offers numerous potential benefits including increased access to care. However, remote cognitive and behavioral assessment also has limitations, and may not be appropriate for certain patients. Currently, evidence‐based guidance on virtual assessment readiness is lacking.

pmc-12392620.title: Optimizing pharmacologic treatment for neonatal opioid withdrawal syndrome (OPTimize NOW): a symptom-based dosing approach study protocol for a multi-center, cluster crossover design randomized controlled trial
pmc-12392620.creator: Leslie W Young, Denise C Babineau, Abhik Das, Sara DeMauro, Walter K Kraft, Scott Lorch, Michele C Walsh, Stephanie Merhar, Lori A Devlin, Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development Neonatal Research and the National Institutes of Health (NIH) Helping to End Addi
pmc-12392620.description: BackgroundOpioid use and misuse during pregnancy rose from 1.5 to 6.5 per 1000 deliveries between 1999 and 2014 and continues as a significant public health concern. A fivefold increase in neonatal opioid withdrawal syndrome (NOWS) has accompanied the increase in opioid use.

pmc-13074361.title: Clinically Relevant Doses of Remimazolam Modulate Cardiac Electrophysiology: Late Repolarization Prolongation and Increased Conduction Dispersion With Preserved QTc
pmc-13074361.creator: Zijun Wang, Ying Cao, Gao Su, Yanyan Feng, Rongfeng Yang, Xue Bai, Hong Gao
pmc-13074361.description: BackgroundRemimazolam, an ultra‐short‐acting benzodiazepine with rapid metabolism and cardiovascular stability, is increasingly used for anesthesia, yet its cardiac electrophysiologic effects are incompletely characterized.MethodsWe conducted a multimodal evaluation in Langendorff‐perfused guinea pig hearts and human induced pluripotent stem cell‐derived cardiomyocytes (hiPSC‐CMs), using surface electrocardiogram (ECG), multielectrode mapping, optical mapping, and whole‐cell patch‐clamp across remimazolam doses (0, 1, 2, 3 mg/kg/h).

pmc-13181973.title: The LGR5/TFF2 ratio as a stem cell biomarker predicts high-risk status in chronic atrophic gastritis: a retrospective cohort study
pmc-13181973.creator: Qingqing Zhang, Di Wu, Fengyun Guo, Shengnan Yang, Lijing Bao, Ruiying Zhang, Ping Wang
pmc-13181973.description: BackgroundChronic atrophic gastritis (CAG) severity risk assessment remains challenging due to limitations of current static histologic/endoscopic tools. We evaluated the leucine-rich repeat-containing G-protein coupled receptor 5 (LGR5)/trefoil factor 2 (TFF2) ratio — quantifying gastric stem cell niche imbalance— as a dynamic biomarker for high-risk CAG (OLGA/OLGIM III-IV).

pmc-13371662.title: Retrospective evaluation of clinical performance of three measurement catheter fixation methods in urodynamic studies
pmc-13371662.creator: Xiao Zeng, Zhihui Huang, Hong Shen, De-yi Luo, Tao Jin
pmc-13371662.description: BackgroundCatheter displacement during urodynamic studies remains a common challenge, potentially introducing artifacts, compromising test accuracy, and decreasing patient comfort. Despite the clinical significance of stable catheter fixation, evidence-based recommendations for optimal fixation techniques are lacking. This study seeks to address this gap by comparing the effectiveness and patient comfort associated with three commonly used catheter fixation methods during urodynamic study.

pmc-13619335.title: Response to “Caution: Fundamental data quality issues underlying intelligent prediction of enzyme optimal pH”
pmc-13619335.creator: Sizhe Qiu, Aidong Yang
pmc-13619335.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). We respond to concerns regarding fundamental data quality issues in datasets used for machine learning prediction of enzyme optimal pH (pHopt). We re-examined six questioned protein entries by tracing their annotated pH values to the original literature. Our analysis confirmed substantial discrepancies for several entries, including incorrect experimental values, misassigned protein identities, and proteins lacking the reported catalytic activity, whereas one entry was consistent with the literature. These findings support the need for rigorous verification of biochemical data underlying predictive models.
